classification.difficultyReason: Every part is a single linear absolute-value inequality solved by the taught two-case method. The hardest parts, such as |4x-3|>5 and |5x+4|>=6, need only one split into cases, simple rearrangement and a choice between 'and' and 'or'. This is slightly above p16-q1, where the graph does the reading, because the student must now pick the case structure and the direction of the sign flip without a graph. It stays below the routine linked procedures of p5-q2 and p17-q4, which add sketching, fractional forms or other extra steps.

classification.difficultyReason: The student must recognise the special cases where the right-hand side is zero or negative. Using |u|>=0, they decide between all reals, a single point, all reals except a point, or no solution, rather than running the usual two-case split. The parts need almost no algebra, but the student has to interpret what the inequality means and pick the right case, which goes beyond reading a supplied graph in p16-q1. There is no multi-step linked procedure, rational function or sketching of the kind in p5-q2, so it sits below that.
